messages:
ACME-app: Hey team — we started seeing a spike this morning and then ~2% of requests started returning 429s after the client failed over to a second region. Primary kept returning 200s for the same requests. This looks like regional capacity exhaustion + failover behavior. Can you help triage?

ACME-app: Repro steps we took: 1) ramp traffic from 200 -> 3000 rps over 30s; 2) client library configured with prefer-region: us-east-1, failover allowed to us-west-2; 3) after ~20s, about ~2% of requests started 429ing and had `retry_after` headers. Example failing curl:```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-xxx"
  -H "x-prefer-region: us-east-1"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-13b","input":"hello"}'
```
Response sample:```json
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: rq_01G8Q...
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "retry_after": 3,
  "region": "us-west-2"
}
```
We also saw mixed latencies — the ones that failed had very short server processing times (i.e., immediate reject) while successful ones had normal token times. Not seeing auth or billing errors.

Samira: Thanks, sorry you're hitting this — we'll investigate. A few quick q's: which deployment tier is this on (hosted/dedicated/private)? can you paste the `X-Request-Id` from a few 429 responses? Also, do you have a traffic window we can use to reproduce? :eyes:

ACME-app: Hosted. I grabbed a few ids: `rq_01G8QAAA`, `rq_01G8QBBB`, `rq_01G8QCCC`. We can reproduce with the same ramp profile — will keep it running for the next 10m.

Jorge: Pinging SRE on this. Initial hypothesis: primary region hit its per-region quota and the routing logic attempted failover, but the target region only has a small "cross-region borrow" allowance. Once that borrow bucket is consumed, additional routed requests are rejected with 429 rather than queued. That matches the short reject times.

Jorge: What to collect for us: 1) the `X-Request-Id` (you have them) 2) the customer id (account id) 3) peak per-second token and request rates during the spike (app-side) 4) attach a capture of the failing response headers. With that we can look up the routing decision in the infra logs.

Samira: Fast mitigation options: - client-side: add exponential backoff with jitter and cap max concurrent requests per connection (we recommend <= 250 parallel requests per API key for hosted unless you have Dedicated). - short-term: we can pin this account to prefer us-east-1 only (disable failover) so you won't bounce to a smaller capacity region — that reduces availability but avoids cross-region 429s. - support option: request temporary quota bump for the window (requires ops approval).

Nina: Quick note on product behavior: we intentionally reject on the target region if borrow allowance is exhausted to keep tail latency predictable for local tenants. Failover does not magically double capacity — failover respects per-region hard caps + borrow policy. Borrow policy config looks like:```yaml
routing:
  failover_enabled: true
  borrow_pct_per_request: 0.2  # up to 20% of target pool can be used for cross-region overflow
  burst_token_refill_sec: 60
  max_failover_inflight: 500
```
So in practice a big surge will exhaust those burst tokens quickly.

Jorge: How we debug from infra: run `ri-ctl` to fetch per-region pool usage and borrow bucket state. Example internal commands (SRE-only):```bash
ri-ctl pool show --customer acme-123 --region us-east-1
ri-ctl pool show --customer acme-123 --region us-west-2
ri-ctl borrow-status --customer acme-123
```
If you can't run those, paste one of the `X-Request-Id`s and we'll pull logs for the routing decisions.

ACME-app: Here's one full raw response I captured (headers + body):```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:12:03 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: rq_01G8QAAA
X-Region: us-west-2
X-RateLimit-Limit: 3000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1678450323

{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":4}
```

Samira: got it. Passing to ops to check borrow bucket. @Jorge can you pull the routing trace for `rq_01G8QAAA`?

Jorge: On it. Quick pointer for the customer if you want to reproduce with lower blast radius: use `hey` or `wrk` to ramp to N rps but set `-c` (concurrency) reasonably. Example command to generate similar pattern:```bash
hey -n 60000 -c 800 -q 200 -z 30s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-xxx" -H "x-prefer-region: us-east-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
This will spike and show the borrow exhaustion behavior.

triage-bot: ticket created: #SUP-98712 — escalation queued to infra and product teams.

Nina: If this is a recurring workload pattern, we should discuss Dedicated reservations or regional capacity reservations for ACME. Dedicated customers can get predictable throughput without relying on borrow tokens. For hosted customers we can also offer a scheduled capacity bump for known traffic windows.

Samira: Ops update (summary): borrow bucket for acme-123 in us-west-2 hit 0 at 15:12:02 UTC. We saw ~15s of steady failed failover attempts after that. No auth or billing issues. We're approving a short temp bump of +30% on borrow allowance for the next 20 minutes to help the in-flight load finish; I'll follow up with the formal change log.

ACME-app: thank you! Can you also confirm whether the client should expect 429s during normal failovers (i.e., is this expected behavior)? We want to decide whether to change client retry logic vs pinning region permanently.

Nina: Short answer: yes, some 429s are expected during aggressive failover scenarios on hosted tier. The routing tries to protect regional tail latency and local SLAs. Best practices: - add client retries with backoff + jitter - cap concurrent outstanding requests per API key - if you have steady high qps, consider Dedicated or scheduled bump - if you want maximum availability at cost of some latency, pin failover but accept regional outage risk

Samira: Next steps: 1) ACME to attach any additional `X-Request-Id` hits and a short traffic profile (rps over time). 2) We applied a temporary borrow bump — monitor and let us know if you still see 429s in the next 10m. 3) We will follow up with a postmortem entry describing borrow bucket tuning and a long-term recommendation.

ACME-app: attaching CSV of rps/time and a couple more request ids. Thanks for the quick turnaround — will report back in 10m. :thumbsup:

triage-bot: update: ticket #SUP-98712 now assigned to infra-ops and product-routing.

Jorge: added internal log refs for the pulled traces: `trace:rt-20260310-5b1f` and `trace:rt-20260310-5b2c`. We'll correlate and add to the ticket.

Samira: closing the thread here for now — reopening if 429s persist after the temporary bump. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
